subject: Throughput entitlement amendment & launch cadence alignment — ArborPay pilot
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput entitlement amendment & launch cadence alignment — ArborPay pilot

Team —

Quick summary: ArborPay confirmed a limited pilot for their payments reconciliation feature starting 2027-11-22. They expect steady traffic early in the day and two predictable peak windows: 11:30–12:15 PT and 20:00–21:00 PT. Current ask from the AE/Customer: temporary increase to throughput entitlement (concurrency & QPS) for the pilot window + a one-week warmup.

Key numbers from the attached forecast (ArborPay-pilot-traffic.xlsx):
- steady-state: ~180 RPS
- working average tokens/request: 450 tokens (most requests are 3 short instructions + 1 summarization response)
- expected burst multiplier: up to 2.5x for 8–12 minute spikes (not sustained)
- pilot duration: 2027-11-22 -> 2027-12-06 (first fortnight)

Asks:
1) Product: any product-level guardrails we need to change for prefix caching / KV lifetime? Is a temporary routing policy (pin to a model variant) needed to stabilize latency?
2) Infra/SRE: recommended temporary entitlement numbers (concurrency & rate), fallback plan if Dedicated capacity spikes or we need to route to lower-cost variants. Also need a short runbook to hand to CS/SEs.
3) Sales/Finance: confirm if ArborPay will accept a short-term surcharge for burst capacity and sign-off on forecast — Karthik, can you confirm commitment?

Timeline: we need approvals and runbook by EOD 2027-11-10 so CS can schedule a warmup traffic replay on 11/18.

Attachment: ArborPay-pilot-traffic.xlsx (forecast + token distribution)

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
---
Note: bold ask is EOD 11/10 for approvals so we can schedule replay and entitlement change before warmup.
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput entitlement amendment & launch cadence alignment — ArborPay pilot

Sean — thanks for the clear summary. A few product notes and questions below.

1) Prefix/KV caching: we can increase prefix cache TTL for this customer to 600s for the pilot; that will reduce tokens at the generative stage for repeated prompts. Two caveats: (a) cache effectiveness depends on prompt entropy — if they vary prompts heavily, benefit will be limited; (b) product needs an allowlist change before we push the TTL change.

2) Model pinning: recommended to pin them to the smaller g-3.7-medium-quant variant during peak windows and enable automatic fallback to g-3.7-large only for low-latency requests. This preserves cost while keeping a predictable performance envelope.

3) Observability hooks: please add a route-specific sample set (5–10 prompts) we can run during warmup to baseline quality metrics. I can own the eval set.

Questions for infra: can we reserve an egress pool with the suggested numbers below, and is the fallback routing policy configurable quickly?

Irene
Irene Choi
PM, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput entitlement amendment & launch cadence alignment — ArborPay pilot

Team — infra notes and a preliminary entitlement proposal.

Read: I looked at the ArborPay-pilot-traffic.xlsx. Based on 180 RPS steady and 2.5x peak factor, plus 450 tokens/request, the rough capacity envelope for the two peak windows is:
- target provisional entitlement: 450 concurrent requests (this maps to ~450 RPS sustained for short windows given our connection model)
- sustained baseline: 200 concurrent (covers steady-state with a small buffer)
- recommended burst quota policy: configured to allow spikes up to 700 concurrent for up to 15 minutes, with automatic circuit-breaker and telemetry alerting.

Notes and constraints:
- If we route some traffic to a lower memory/quant variant (g-3.7-medium-quant), latency will grow ~40–70ms on median but cost drops ~35% — acceptable trade for non-interactive flows.
- We require a test token and a traffic replay file (TrafficPattern.csv) to run a dry-run on staging. Please provide the replay by 11/16 so we can run two cycles.
- I'll prepare a short runbook (throughput-runbook.pdf) with escalation steps and a rollback plan.

Risk: if burst lasts >20 minutes, autoscaling adds latency as we spin up additional machines. That is the largest risk to SLAs during the pilot.

I'll aim to get the runbook and entitlement change request into the SRE queue today.

—David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput entitlement amendment & launch cadence alignment — ArborPay pilot

Confirming commercial posture from my side: ArborPay has committed to the pilot and a PO for the month of Dec if pilot metrics look good. They are amenable to a short-term burst surcharge (one-time fee) to cover dedicated headroom for the two peak windows.

I discussed Black Friday behavior with the customer — they flagged that on B.F. they might see 3x momentary spikes but not sustained. They prefer we avoid routing to degraded variants during checkout flows — i.e., pin checkout route to lowest-latency variant. We can route reconciliation/background routes to cheaper variants.

I'll capture the surcharge in a quick amendment and circulate for legal sign-off.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@arborpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: ArborPay pilot — quick confirmation of traffic cadence and replay file request

Maria — looping you in so we can finalize the warmup schedule and the traffic replay file. Attached is the traffic template (TrafficPattern.csv). Can you confirm the expected peak windows and, if possible, export a replay for our staging run on 2027-11-18?

Per our internal plan, SRE will provision a provisional entitlement for the pilot (baseline + burst), and Product will pin the checkout route to a low-latency variant. We only need your confirmation on two items by EOD 11/12:
1) Confirmed peak windows (local time)
2) TrafficPattern.csv populated with 24 hours of event timestamps during a representative high-day

Attachment: TrafficPattern.csv (template)

Thanks —
Sean
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@arborpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@arborpay.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 15:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ArborPay pilot — quick confirmation of traffic cadence and replay file request

Sean — thanks for the note. Confirming:
- Peak windows (PT): 11:30–12:15 and 20:00–21:00 (matches your summary)
- We attached a behavior export (TrafficPattern.csv) with a representative high-day and a 2x and 3x multiplier column for burst simulation.

We agree to the short-term surcharge for the extra headroom for the pilot; Karthik and I will finalize the amendment this week.

Best,
Maria Torres
Head of Integrations, ArborPay
Attachment: TrafficPattern.csv (producer stub)
